separable: separable — *back up your claim*, and *back me up*; with a pronoun it must split: ✗ *back up me*
gloss: To support someone or confirm what they say.
examples: Will you *back* me *up* if she asks?
Nobody *backed* him *up* in the meeting.
Two witnesses have *backed up* her story.

ru: сдавать назад, сдать назад; пятиться, попятиться
separable: separable when it takes an object — *back the truck up*, *back up the truck*; usually it takes none at all: *back up a little*
transitivity: both — intransitive (back up slowly), transitive (back the car up)
gloss: To move a vehicle or yourself backward.
examples: *Back up* a little — you're too close to the garage.
He *backed* the truck *up* to the loading dock.
She was *backing up* when she hit the mailbox.

ru: делать резервную копию, сделать резервную копию
separable: separable — *back up your photos*, and *back them up*
transitivity: both — transitive (back up the files), intransitive (the laptop is backing up)
gloss: To save a second copy of computer files in case the first is lost.
examples: *Back up* your files before the update.
I *backed* everything *up* to an external drive.
The laptop is *backing up* right now.

separable: separable when there is an object — *backed traffic up*, *backed up traffic*; most often there is none: *the drain backed up*
transitivity: both — intransitive (traffic backs up), transitive (the wreck backed traffic up)
gloss: To pile up and stop moving, the way traffic or water in a clogged drain does.
examples: Traffic *backs up* on this bridge every morning.
The kitchen sink *backed up* again.
The accident *backed* traffic *up* for six miles.

ru: отступать, отступить; идти на попятную, пойти на попятную
separable: no object — nothing can come between *back* and *down*; what you give up on follows the particle: *back down from a threat*
gloss: To stop insisting on something after someone opposes you.
examples: He never *backs down* in an argument.
The company *backed down* after the boycott.
She has refused to *back down*, even with the numbers against her.

separable: inseparable on the rare occasions it takes an object — *back off the deadline*, never ✗ *back the deadline off*; normally it takes none
transitivity: both — intransitive (just back off), transitive (they backed off the demand)
gloss: To stop pressuring or crowding someone and move away.
examples: *Back off* and let him finish.
The dog *backed off* as soon as I stood up.
They have *backed off* their demand for an apology.

ru: отказываться, отказаться (от сделки); идти на попятную
separable: no object — what you withdraw from follows the particle: *back out of the contract*, never ✗ *back the contract out*
gloss: To withdraw from something you had agreed to do.
examples: They *backed out* two days before the closing.
He is *backing out* of the deal.
She has *backed out* of every plan we've made.

separable: separable — *bail out the airline*, and *bail them out*
gloss: To rescue a person or a company from trouble, usually with money.
examples: The government *bailed out* the banks.
My parents *bailed* me *out* again.
Nobody is going to *bail* this company *out*.

ru: выпрыгивать с парашютом, выпрыгнуть; сматываться, смотаться
separable: no object — *bail out*; what you escape takes *of*: *bail out of the deal*
gloss: To jump from an aircraft, or to get out of a situation before it goes bad.
examples: The pilot *bailed out* just before the crash.
He *bails out* whenever the work gets hard.
Two investors have *bailed out* since Tuesday.

separable: inseparable — *bail on your friends*, never ✗ *bail your friends on*
gloss: To abandon a person or a plan at the last minute.
examples: He *bailed on* us an hour before dinner.
She *bails on* every plan we make.
I can't believe they're *bailing on* the trip.

separable: separable when it has an object — *balance out the loss*, *balance it out*; it also works with none: *it all balanced out*
transitivity: both — transitive (balance out the cost), intransitive (it balances out)
gloss: To make two opposite things equal, or to become equal.
examples: The extra shifts *balance out* the slow weeks.
It all *balanced out* in the end.
The two costs are *balancing* each other *out*.

separable: no object — *band together*; who you join takes *with*: *band together with the other tenants*
gloss: To join with other people in order to act as a group.
examples: The neighbors *banded together* to fight the permit.
Small growers are *banding together*.
When money is tight, families *band together*.

separable: separable — *bang up the fender*, and *bang it up*
gloss: To damage something, or injure a part of the body, by hitting it.
examples: He *banged up* the car in the parking garage.
She *bangs* her knee *up* on that shelf every single week.
The rental was already *banged up* when we got it.

ru: строчить, настрочить; быстро делать, быстро сделать
separable: separable — *bang out a draft*, and *bang it out*
gloss: To produce something quickly and without much care.
examples: She *banged out* the report in an hour.
He *bangs out* three songs a week.
I'm *banging out* an email and then we can go.

separable: inseparable — *bank on a raise*, never ✗ *bank a raise on*
gloss: To depend on something happening.
examples: Don't *bank on* the weather holding.
We *banked on* a quiet summer and got the opposite.
They're *banking on* him to close the deal.

ru: ожидать, ожидать заранее; предвидеть, предвидеть заранее
separable: inseparable — *bargain for trouble*, never ✗ *bargain trouble for*; it lives mostly in the phrase *more than I bargained for*
gloss: To expect something, almost always in a sentence saying you did not.
examples: That was more than I *bargained for*.
She got more trouble than she had *bargained for*.
Nobody *bargains for* a flat tire in the rain.

separable: no object — *barge in*; what you interrupt takes *on*: *barge in on a meeting*
gloss: To enter or interrupt rudely, without being invited.
examples: He *barged in* without knocking.
She *barges in* whenever she feels like it.
Sorry for *barging in* on your call.

separable: separable — *bawl out the kid*, and *bawl him out*
gloss: To scold someone loudly and angrily.
examples: The coach *bawled* him *out* in front of everyone.
She *bawls out* the whole crew when the orders are late.
I got *bawled out* for being ten minutes late.

separable: separable — *beef up the staff*, and *beef it up*
gloss: To make something stronger, bigger, or more effective.
examples: They *beefed up* security after the break-in.
We need to *beef* the ending *up*.
The airline is *beefing up* its winter schedule.

ru: петь во весь голос, спеть во весь голос; горланить
separable: separable — *belt out a song*, and *belt it out*
gloss: To sing or play something very loudly.
examples: She *belted out* the national anthem.
He *belts out* show tunes in the shower.
The band was *belting out* an old Motown number.

ru: терять сознание, потерять сознание; отключаться, отключиться
separable: no object — *black out*; there is nothing to place between the two words
gloss: To lose consciousness, or to lose all memory of a period of time.
examples: He *blacked out* for a few seconds.
I *black out* if I stand up too fast.
She had *blacked out* before the ambulance arrived.

separable: separable — *black out the city*, and *black it out*
gloss: To cut the power to a place, or to make it completely dark.
examples: The storm *blacked out* half the county.
They're *blacking* the windows *out* for the show.
Three neighborhoods were *blacked out* until Tuesday.

separable: separable — *black out the names*, and *black them out*
gloss: To cover written words with ink so that they cannot be read.
examples: The agency *blacked out* every name in the file.
Someone had *blacked* the address *out* with a marker.
They're *blacking out* the sensitive parts before release.

ru: забывать начисто, забыть начисто; отключаться, отключиться
separable: no object — *blank out*; what you cannot recall takes *on*: *blank out on her name*
gloss: To suddenly be unable to remember something you know.
examples: I *blanked out* in the middle of the exam.
She *blanks out* whenever someone raises their voice.
He was *blanking out* on her name the whole evening.

separable: no object — *blast off*; nothing can sit between the two words
gloss: For a rocket to leave the ground.
examples: The rocket *blasted off* at dawn.
The shuttle *blasts off* on Thursday.
We watched it *blast off* from the beach.

separable: no object — *blend in*; what you match takes *with*: *blend in with the crowd*
gloss: To look or behave enough like everything around you that nobody notices you.
examples: He tried to *blend in* with the locals.
The new couch *blends in* nicely.
She was *blending in* until she opened her mouth.

separable: separable — *block off the road*, and *block it off*
gloss: To close an area so that nobody can get through it.
examples: Police *blocked off* the street.
They're *blocking off* the whole block for the parade.
We *blocked* the stairs *off* with a baby gate.

separable: separable — *block out the sun*, and *block it out*
gloss: To stop light, noise, or an unwanted thought from getting through.
examples: Heavy curtains *block out* the light.
She *blocked out* the noise with headphones.
He has *blocked out* most of that year.

separable: separable — *block out an afternoon*, and *block it out*
gloss: To set aside a period of time for one purpose.
examples: *Block out* two hours for the review.
I *blocked* Friday morning *out* for the move.
She's *blocking out* time to write.

separable: separable — *block in a car*, and *block it in*; with a pronoun it must split: *they blocked me in*
gloss: To park so close to another car that it cannot get out.
examples: Somebody *blocked* me *in* again.
A delivery truck *blocks in* the whole row every morning.
We were *blocked in* until the driver came back.

ru: заслонять, заслонить; стирать из памяти, стереть
separable: separable — *blot out the light*, and *blot it out*
gloss: To hide something completely from sight, or to push a memory out of your mind.
examples: Clouds *blotted out* the sun.
He tries to *blot out* the memory with work.
The smoke was *blotting out* the whole ridge.

separable: separable — *blurt out the answer*, and *blurt it out*
gloss: To say something suddenly, without stopping to think.
examples: She *blurted out* the price before he could stop her.
He *blurts out* whatever he's thinking.
I didn't mean to, but I *blurted* it *out*.

separable: separable — *board up the door*, and *board it up*
gloss: To cover a window or door with boards to protect or close a building.
examples: They *boarded up* the windows before the storm.
The store has been *boarded up* for years.
He's *boarding* the place *up* this weekend.

separable: separable when it has an object — *bog the team down*, *bog down the team*; often there is none: *the project bogged down*
transitivity: both — intransitive (the talks bogged down), transitive (the paperwork bogged us down)
gloss: To get stuck in detail or difficulty so that no progress is made.
examples: The talks *bogged down* over money.
Don't let the details *bog* you *down*.
The project has *bogged down* completely.

separable: inseparable — nothing can split the three words: *it boils down to money*, never ✗ *it boils money down to*
gloss: To have one simple thing as the real point, once everything else is stripped away.
examples: It all *boils down to* money.
The argument *boiled down to* one word.
What it's *boiling down to* is a question of trust.

ru: вскипать, вскипеть; перерастать в скандал, перерасти
separable: no object — *boil over*; there is nothing to place between the two words
gloss: For anger or tension to break out into open conflict.
examples: The argument *boiled over* in the parking lot.
Tensions *boil over* every August.
Things had been *boiling over* long before anyone called the police.

separable: inseparable — *bone up on the rules*, never ✗ *bone the rules up on*
gloss: To study a subject hard in a short time, usually before a test or a meeting.
examples: I need to *bone up on* my Spanish before the trip.
He *boned up on* tax law over the weekend.
She's *boning up on* the case files tonight.

separable: separable when it has an object — *boot the server up*, *boot up the server*; it also works with none: *the laptop booted up*
transitivity: both — transitive (boot up the laptop), intransitive (it is booting up)
gloss: To start a computer, or for a computer to start.
examples: *Boot up* the laptop and I'll show you.
The machine *booted up* fine this morning.
It's still *booting up*.

separable: separable — *boot out the manager*, and *boot him out*
gloss: To force someone to leave a job, a school, or a place.
examples: The board *booted* him *out* in March.
They're *booting out* two more members this week.
He got *booted out* of the program.

separable: separable — *boss around the interns*, and *boss them around*; with a pronoun it must split: ✗ *boss around me*
gloss: To keep telling someone what to do in a way they resent.
examples: She *bosses* everyone *around*.
Stop *bossing* me *around*.
He *bossed around* the new hires all summer.

separable: separable — *bottle up your feelings*, and *bottle them up*
gloss: To keep a strong feeling inside instead of showing it.
examples: He *bottles up* everything until he explodes.
She *bottled up* her anger for years.
You've been *bottling* it *up* too long.

ru: достигать дна, достичь дна; опускаться до низшей точки
separable: no object — *bottom out*; nothing can sit between the two words
gloss: To reach the lowest point before starting to rise again.
examples: Prices *bottomed out* in April.
The market seems to be *bottoming out*.
Sales *bottom out* every January.

separable: no object — *bounce back*; what you recover from takes *from*: *bounce back from a loss*
gloss: To return to a normal, healthy, or successful state after trouble.
examples: She *bounced back* after a rough year.
The team *bounces back* fast.
He's *bouncing back* from the surgery.

ru: советоваться, посоветоваться (об идее); обкатывать идею на ком-то
separable: separable — and here it must split, because the idea goes in the middle: *bounce it off her*, never ✗ *bounce off her the idea*
gloss: To tell someone an idea in order to hear what they think of it.
examples: Can I *bounce* an idea *off* you?
She *bounced* the plan *off* her lawyer first.
We've been *bouncing* names *off* each other all week.

ru: уходить, уйти (с поста); откланяться, выходить из игры
separable: no object — *bow out*; what you leave takes *of*: *bow out of the race*
gloss: To withdraw from a job or a contest, usually quietly and by choice.
examples: He *bowed out* of the race in May.
She *bows out* gracefully every time.
Two sponsors have *bowed out*.

separable: separable — *bowl over the audience*, and *bowl them over*
gloss: To surprise or impress someone so much that they hardly know what to say.
examples: The news *bowled* me *over*.
She *bowls over* everyone she meets.
We were *bowled over* by how kind they were.

ru: зажимать, зажать; загонять в угол, загнать в угол
separable: separable — *box in a runner*, and *box him in*
gloss: To trap someone so that they have no room to move or no choice left.
examples: The truck *boxed* us *in* at the light.
The contract *boxes in* the new manager.
She felt *boxed in* by the deadline.

ru: расширяться, расшириться; осваивать новое направление, освоить
separable: no object — *branch out*; the new area takes *into*: *branch out into catering*
gloss: To start doing something new, beyond what you already do.
examples: The bakery *branched out* into catering.
She wants to *branch out* on her own.
They're *branching out* into new markets.

separable: no object of its own — *branch off*; the road or topic you leave follows the particle: *branch off the highway*
gloss: To split away from a main road, line, or subject and go a different way.
examples: The trail *branches off* just past the bridge.
We *branched off* the main road too early.
The conversation kept *branching off* into other things.

ru: легко справляться, легко справиться; проходить играючи
separable: inseparable — *breeze through the exam*, never ✗ *breeze the exam through*
gloss: To do something difficult easily and quickly.
examples: She *breezed through* the interview.
He *breezes through* every test.
They're *breezing through* the first round.

separable: separable when it has an object — *brighten up the room*, *brighten it up*; it also works with none: *she brightened up*
transitivity: both — transitive (brighten up the office), intransitive (her face brightened up)
gloss: To become more cheerful, or to make a place or a mood more cheerful.
examples: Flowers would *brighten up* the room.
Her face *brightened up* when she saw him.
The sky is finally *brightening up*.

separable: separable — *brush off the question*, and *brush it off*
gloss: To refuse to take a person or a concern seriously.
examples: He *brushed off* the criticism.
She *brushes* me *off* every time I bring it up.
They have *brushed off* every warning.

separable: separable — *brush aside the objection*, and *brush it aside*
gloss: To dismiss an objection or a difficulty as unimportant.
examples: The judge *brushed aside* the objection.
He *brushes aside* anything he doesn't want to hear.
Her concerns were *brushed aside* in one sentence.

ru: освежать в памяти, освежить; подтягивать, подтянуть
separable: inseparable — *brush up on your Spanish*, never ✗ *brush your Spanish up on*
gloss: To practice something you once knew well so that it comes back.
examples: I should *brush up on* my French.
He *brushed up on* the rules before the game.
She's *brushing up on* her interview answers.

ru: браться за дело, взяться за дело всерьёз
separable: no object — *buckle down*; the work takes *to*: *buckle down to studying*
gloss: To start working seriously after wasting time.
examples: It's time to *buckle down* and study.
He finally *buckled down* in March.
They're *buckling down* for the last week of the quarter.

separable: no object — *buckle up*; to strap someone else in, Americans say *buckle the kids in*
gloss: To fasten your seat belt.
examples: *Buckle up* — we're leaving.
She *buckled up* and started the engine.
Nobody was *buckling up* in those days.

ru: не выдерживать, не выдержать (давления); ломаться, сломаться
separable: no object — *buckle under*; what crushes you follows the particle: *buckle under the pressure*
gloss: To give way under pressure instead of holding out.
examples: He *buckled under* the pressure in the final round.
Most witnesses *buckle under* that kind of questioning.
She has never *buckled under*, not once.

separable: no object — *bulk up*; nothing sits between the two words
gloss: To put on muscle and body weight on purpose.
examples: He *bulked up* over the winter.
She's *bulking up* for the season.
Linemen *bulk up* in the off-season.

separable: separable — *bum out the whole team*, and *bum them out*
gloss: To make someone sad or disappointed — informal.
examples: That news really *bummed* me *out*.
It *bums* her *out* to think about it.
We were all *bummed out* by the cancellation.

separable: inseparable when it names a place — *bum around Europe*, never ✗ *bum Europe around*; often it takes no object at all
transitivity: both — intransitive (bum around all day), transitive (bum around Mexico)
gloss: To spend time doing nothing in particular, or to travel with no plan — informal.
examples: They *bummed around* Europe for a year.
He *bums around* the house all day.
We spent August *bumming around*.

ru: случайно встречать, случайно встретить; натыкаться на, наткнуться на
separable: inseparable — *bump into an old friend*, never ✗ *bump an old friend into*
gloss: To meet someone by chance.
examples: I *bumped into* your brother at the store.
She *bumps into* him at the gym all the time.
We kept *bumping into* each other all week.

separable: separable — *bump up the rent*, and *bump it up*
gloss: To increase an amount, a price, or a position.
examples: They *bumped up* the price again.
The airline *bumped* us *up* to first class.
She's *bumping up* the deadline by a week.

separable: separable — *bump off a rival*, and *bump him off*
gloss: To murder someone — slang, heard mostly in crime stories.
examples: Somebody *bumped off* the witness.
In the movie he gets *bumped off* in the first ten minutes.
They were *bumping off* rivals one by one.

ru: тепло одеваться, тепло одеться; укутывать, укутать
separable: separable when it has an object — *bundle up the kids*, *bundle them up*; usually it takes none: *bundle up, it's freezing*
transitivity: both — intransitive (bundle up before you go), transitive (bundle the baby up)
gloss: To dress in warm clothes, or to dress someone else in them.
examples: *Bundle up* — it's ten degrees out.
She *bundled* the kids *up* and walked them to school.
We were *bundled up* in every coat we owned.

separable: no object — *butt in*; the conversation takes *on*: *butt in on their argument*
gloss: To interrupt a conversation or interfere where you were not asked.
examples: He *butts in* every time she speaks.
Sorry to *butt in*, but the car is here.
She *butted in* before I finished.

ru: не лезть, отстать; не вмешиваться, не вмешаться
separable: no object — *butt out*; what you drop takes *of*: *butt out of my finances*
gloss: To stop interfering in something that is not your business.
examples: *Butt out* — this isn't your business.
He finally *butted out*.
I told her to *butt out* of my finances.

separable: separable — *butter up the boss*, and *butter him up*
gloss: To flatter someone because you want something from them.
examples: He's been *buttering up* the boss all week.
She *buttered* him *up* before asking for the day off.
Don't try to *butter* me *up*.

ru: доводить до конца, довести до конца; утрясать, утрясти
separable: separable — *button up the deal*, and *button it up*
gloss: To settle the last details of something and close it out.
examples: Let's *button up* the contract today.
They *buttoned up* the last details on Friday.
We're *buttoning* everything *up* before the holiday.

separable: separable — *buzz in the delivery guy*, and *buzz him in*; with a pronoun it must split: ✗ *buzz in me*
gloss: To open a locked building door for someone by pressing a button inside.
examples: *Buzz* me *in* — I'm at the door.
She *buzzed* him *in* without asking who it was.
The doorman *buzzes in* anyone with a badge.
